title: CBSE CLASS 7 — English | Sentence Transformation
description: Subject-wise test on Sentence Transformation (English) for CBSE CLASS 7. 25Q.
subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct indirect speech form of the sentence: *He said, 'I have finished my work.'*

options.text: He said that I have finished my work.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he' to match the subject of the reporting verb.

options.text: He said that he had finished his work.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: present perfect tense changes to past perfect, and pronouns are adjusted.

options.text: He said that he finished his work.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect ('had finished') instead of simple past.

options.text: He said I finished my work.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he', and the tense should be past perfect.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the present perfect tense ('have finished') changes to past perfect ('had finished') and the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' to match the subject of the reporting verb.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tense and pronouns appropriately when converting direct speech to indirect speech.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Identify the correct active voice form of the sentence: *The poem was written by Tagore.*

options.text: Tagore has written the poem.
options.explanation: The tense should be simple past ('wrote') instead of present perfect ('has written').

options.text: Tagore wrote the poem.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: the subject 'Tagore' performs the action in simple past tense.

options.text: Tagore was writing the poem.
options.explanation: The tense should be simple past ('wrote') instead of past continuous ('was writing').

options.text: The poem is being written by Tagore.
options.explanation: This is still in passive voice, not active.

questions.explanation: The given sentence is in passive voice. Changing it to active voice requires the subject ('Tagore') to perform the action, using the simple past tense ('wrote').
questions.hint: The subject of the passive sentence becomes the doer in the active voice.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Choose the correct transformation of the sentence from direct to indirect speech: *She said, 'Can you help me?'*

options.text: She asked if I can help her.
options.explanation: The modal 'can' should change to 'could' in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked if I could help her.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: 'can' changes to 'could', and 'you' changes to 'I'.

options.text: She asked if you could help her.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'you' should change to 'I' to match the reported context.

options.text: She asked can I help her.
options.explanation: The sentence structure is incorrect for indirect speech.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the modal 'can' changes to 'could' and the pronoun 'you' changes to 'I' to maintain the meaning in the reported context.
questions.hint: Modal verbs like 'can' change to their past forms ('could') in indirect speech.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly transforms the given sentence into a negative form? *He has been reading this book for two hours.*

options.text: He hasn’t been reading this book for two hours.
options.explanation: Correct negative form: 'hasn’t' + 'been' + '-ing' form of the verb.

options.text: He hasn’t read this book for two hours.
options.explanation: This changes the tense to present perfect simple instead of present perfect continuous.

options.text: He didn’t read this book for two hours.
options.explanation: This changes the tense to simple past, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

options.text: He was not reading this book for two hours.
options.explanation: This changes the tense to past continuous, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: The correct negative form of the present perfect continuous tense ('has been reading') uses 'hasn’t' and retains the '-ing' form of the verb.
questions.hint: The negative form of present perfect continuous uses 'hasn’t' or 'haven’t' followed by 'been' and the '-ing' form of the verb.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: The sentence *She said to me, 'Do not disturb me.'* is transformed into indirect speech as:

options.text: She told me not to disturb her.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: 'told' + 'not to' + base form of the verb ('disturb').

options.text: She told me do not disturb her.
options.explanation: The structure is incorrect; 'do not' should be replaced with 'not to'.

options.text: She said to me not to disturb her.
options.explanation: The reporting verb should be 'told' instead of 'said' for imperative sentences.

options.text: She told me that I should not disturb her.
options.explanation: This is not the correct transformation for an imperative sentence.

questions.explanation: The imperative sentence in direct speech ('Do not disturb me') is transformed into indirect speech using 'told + not + to-infinitive' form.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in direct speech are transformed using 'told' or 'asked' followed by 'not to' and the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Identify the correct indirect speech form of the sentence: *The teacher said, 'The Earth revolves around the Sun.'*

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
options.explanation: The tense should not change for general truths; 'revolved' is incorrect.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: the tense remains present simple for general truths.

options.text: The teacher said the Earth is revolving around the Sun.
options.explanation: The tense should remain present simple, not present continuous.

options.text: The teacher said the Earth was revolving around the Sun.
options.explanation: The tense should remain present simple, not past continuous.

questions.explanation: When reporting a general truth or scientific fact in indirect speech, the tense does not change. Hence, 'revolves' remains in the present simple tense.
questions.hint: General truths and scientific facts retain their tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which option correctly transforms the following sentence into its interrogative form? *She can swim across the river.*

options.text: Can she swim across the river?
options.explanation: Correct interrogative form: modal 'can' is placed before the subject 'she'.

options.text: Does she can swim across the river?
options.explanation: The structure is incorrect; 'can' is a modal verb and does not take 'do'.

options.text: Is she able to swim across the river?
options.explanation: This is a correct transformation but not the simplest interrogative form using 'can'.

options.text: She can swim across the river?
options.explanation: This is not a correct interrogative form; it lacks inversion.

questions.explanation: The interrogative form of a modal verb sentence places the modal ('can') before the subject ('she').
questions.hint: For sentences with modal verbs, the interrogative form is formed by inverting the modal and the subject.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Assertion: The sentence *He asked, 'Where are you going?'* transforms into indirect speech as *He asked where I was going.* Reason: In indirect speech, the question word ('where') is retained, and the tense shifts from present continuous ('are going') to past continuous ('was going').

options.text: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.explanation: The assertion is correct, and the reason correctly explains the transformation.

options.text: Both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: Assertion is true, but the reason is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: Assertion is false, but the reason is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is correct, and the reason correctly explains the transformation of the sentence into indirect speech.
questions.hint: Both the assertion and the reason must be evaluated for correctness and whether the reason explains the assertion.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Case-Based: Ravi said to his friend, 'I will meet you at the park tomorrow.' Which of the following is the correct indirect speech form?

options.text: Ravi told his friend that he would meet him at the park the next day.
options.explanation: Correct transformation: 'will meet' changes to 'would meet', and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.

options.text: Ravi said to his friend that he will meet him at the park tomorrow.
options.explanation: The tense should change to conditional ('would meet'), and 'tomorrow' should change to 'the next day'.

options.text: Ravi told his friend I would meet you at the park the next day.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he' to match the subject of the reporting verb.

options.text: Ravi told his friend that he meets him at the park tomorrow.
options.explanation: The tense should change to conditional ('would meet'), and 'tomorrow' should change to 'the next day'.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the future tense ('will meet') changes to conditional ('would meet'), and time expressions like 'tomorrow' change to 'the next day.'
questions.hint: Future tense in direct speech changes to conditional in indirect speech, and time expressions are adjusted accordingly.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly transforms the given sentence into passive voice? *The children are playing football in the park.*

options.text: Football is being played by the children in the park.
options.explanation: Correct passive form: 'football' is the subject, and 'is being played' indicates present continuous passive.

options.text: Football is played by the children in the park.
options.explanation: This is passive simple present, not present continuous.

options.text: The children are playing football by the park.
options.explanation: This is still in active voice, not passive.

options.text: Football was being played by the children in the park.
options.explanation: This changes the tense to past continuous, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: The correct passive form uses 'is being played' to indicate the present continuous tense in passive voice, with 'football' as the subject.
questions.hint: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject in the passive voice, and the verb is adjusted to the passive form.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: *He said, 'I am reading a book.'*

options.text: He said that he was reading a book.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of tense and pronoun.

options.text: He said that I am reading a book.
options.explanation: Pronoun 'I' should change to 'he'.

options.text: He said that he is reading a book.
options.explanation: Tense should shift to past continuous.

options.text: He said that he has been reading a book.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense shift.

questions.explanation: The tense shifts from present continuous ('am reading') to past continuous ('was reading') in indirect speech. Also, the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' to maintain consistency.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tense and adjust the pronoun.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Select the correct transformation of the following sentence into passive voice: *The teacher punished the students.*

options.text: The students were punished by the teacher.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice transformation.

options.text: The students punished the teacher.
options.explanation: Active voice, not passive.

options.text: The teacher was punished by the students.
options.explanation: Incorrect subject and object reversal.

options.text: The students are punished by the teacher.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense used.

questions.explanation: In passive voice, the object ('the students') becomes the subject, and the verb is changed to 'were punished.' The original subject ('the teacher') becomes the agent introduced by 'by.'
questions.hint: Identify the object and subject, then convert the verb to passive form.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Choose the appropriate indirect speech for the sentence: *She said, 'Where is the station?'*

options.text: She asked where the station was.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of question to indirect speech.

options.text: She asked where was the station.
options.explanation: Incorrect word order in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked where is the station.
options.explanation: Verb tense should shift to past.

options.text: She asked where has the station been.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and structure.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the question word ('where') comes first, and the verb shifts to past tense ('was'). The structure changes from interrogative to declarative.
questions.hint: Convert the question into a statement and adjust the verb tense.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct direct speech for the sentence: *He told me that he had finished his work.*

options.text: He said to me, 'I have finished my work.'
options.explanation: Correct direct speech transformation.

options.text: He said to me, 'I finished my work.'
options.explanation: Incorrect tense shift.

options.text: He said to me, 'I had finished my work.'
options.explanation: Tense should shift back to present perfect.

options.text: He said, 'I have finished my work.'
options.explanation: Missing 'to me' for consistency.

questions.explanation: The indirect speech 'had finished' shifts back to present perfect ('have finished') in direct speech. The reporting verb 'told' changes to 'said to' in direct speech.
questions.hint: Convert the indirect speech back to direct speech by reversing the tense and reporting verb.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Select the correct transformation of the following sentence into indirect speech: *He said, 'Alas! I have lost my wallet.'*

options.text: He exclaimed sadly that he had lost his wallet.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of exclamation and tense.

options.text: He said that he had lost his wallet.
options.explanation: Missing the exclamation conversion.

options.text: He exclaimed that he lost his wallet.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense shift.

options.text: He said sadly that he has lost his wallet.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and structure.

questions.explanation: The exclamation 'Alas!' is converted to 'exclaimed sadly' in indirect speech. The tense shifts from present perfect ('have lost') to past perfect ('had lost').
questions.hint: Convert the exclamation to an appropriate reporting verb and adjust the tense.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

questions.question: Which option correctly transforms the sentence into passive voice? *Someone has stolen my bicycle.*

options.text: My bicycle has been stolen.
options.explanation: Correct passive voice transformation.

options.text: My bicycle was stolen.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense used.

options.text: My bicycle is stolen.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and structure.

options.text: My bicycle has stolen.
options.explanation: Incorrect verb form.

questions.explanation: The passive voice uses 'has been stolen' to indicate that the focus is on the object ('my bicycle') rather than the doer ('someone').
questions.hint: Focus on the object and use the correct passive verb form.
questions.subject: cbse7-english

options.text: Ravi told his friend that he would meet him at the park after school.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of tense and pronouns.

options.text: Ravi told his friend that he will meet him at the park after school.
options.explanation: Tense should shift to conditional.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense shift.

options.text: Ravi told his friend that he met him at the park after school.

questions.question: Select the correct transformation of the following sentence into active voice: *The cake was baked by my mother.*

options.text: My mother baked the cake.
options.explanation: Correct active voice transformation.

options.text: My mother has baked the cake.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense used.

options.text: The cake is baked by my mother.
options.explanation: Passive voice, not active.

options.text: My mother bakes the cake.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense used.

questions.explanation: In active voice, the subject ('my mother') performs the action, and the verb is in simple past tense ('baked'). The object ('the cake') becomes the subject in passive voice but reverts to object in active voice.

questions.question: Which option correctly transforms the sentence into indirect speech? *He said, 'Do not touch the wire.'*

options.text: He told that do not touch the wire.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure and verb form.

questions.explanation: The imperative sentence ('Do not touch the wire') is transformed into indirect speech using 'advised not to' to maintain the meaning of prohibition.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: He said, 'I have finished my work.'

options.text: He said that he had finished his work.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense; present perfect should become past perfect.

questions.explanation: The correct transformation requires changing the present perfect tense ('have finished') to past perfect ('had finished') and the pronoun 'I' to 'he.' This follows the rule of backshifting in indirect speech.

questions.question: Read the following sentence and choose the correct transformation to indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Complete your assignments before Monday.'

options.text: The teacher told the students to complete their assignments before Monday.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of an imperative sentence into indirect speech.

options.text: The teacher said the students to complete their assignments before Monday.
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb; 'said' should be replaced with 'told' for commands.

options.text: The teacher asked the students to complete their assignments before Monday.
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb; 'asked' is used for questions, not commands.

options.text: The teacher told that the students complete their assignments before Monday.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; 'told' should be followed by an object and an infinitive.

questions.explanation: The imperative sentence 'Complete your assignments...' is correctly transformed into indirect speech using 'told the students to complete...' The pronoun 'your' changes to 'their,' and the reporting verb 'said' is replaced with 'told' to convey the command.
questions.hint: Identify the type of sentence (imperative) and use the appropriate reporting verb and structure for indirect speech.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct indirect speech for the question: 'Where are you going?' she asked me.

options.text: She asked me where I was going.
options.explanation: Correct transformation of a question into indirect speech with proper word order and tense shift.

options.text: She asked me where was I going.
options.explanation: Incorrect word order; the subject and verb should not be inverted in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked me where you are going.
options.explanation: Incorrect pronoun and tense; 'you' should change to 'I,' and the tense should shift to past.

options.text: She asked me where I am going.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense; the present tense should shift to past in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: In transforming a question into indirect speech, the word order changes from 'Where are you going?' to 'where I was going.' The pronoun 'you' changes to 'I,' and the tense shifts from present continuous ('are going') to past continuous ('was going').
questions.hint: Remember to invert the subject and verb in the question and adjust pronouns and tense accordingly.
questions.subject: cbse7-english
